All maps that try to take a 3D globe and place it on a 2D piece of flat paper will be a lie. Only an actual globe will be correct.

All these others are what is called a "projection." The most used projection is the Mercator projection, which was designed to be able to use a straight edge to accurately draw a line for navigation between places. The Peters projection you show here uses a "equal area" projection, based on equalizing the area of a cylinder section to the paper map by doubling the length of the cylinder. This "flattens" the far north and south areas, whereas the Mercator projection enlarged them. This map is no more an accurate depcition of the globe as any other, it just tries to display the relative SIZE of the land by making the middle larger in the projection to denote the larger area covered due to the larger curvature at the equator. However, the equator is just as arbitrary as say, a projection through either the Tropic of capricorn or the Tropic of Cancer - it just has easier math (45 degrees to each side.) But, a map make could take ANY line that is performs the largest circle on the globe, and apply the projection to that, rather than the 0 degree latitude line. If doing it by degrees of angle, you would have 180 different maps using the exact same mathematical computation, with differing results as you flatten those areas on the edges of your cylinder.
